newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unemployment rises in May, reverses decline.
newsitem.headline: French unemployment rises in May, reverses decline.

text.p: French unemployment jumped 1.1 percent in May, reversing three months of declines, figures released on Monday by the employment ministry showed.
The official jobless number climbed 32,400 to 3,113,500 in a stark reminder to France's new Socialist-led government of the uphill task it faces in fulfilling its election pledge to cut unemployment.
The jobless rate, calculated according to International Labour Organisation standards, remained unchanged at 12.5 percent.
The rise was the biggest monthly increase since October 1993, the ministry said. Over one year, the number of job seekers has risen 2.3 percent.
Some economists called the jump a big surprise, saying that financial markets had been expecting unemployment to remain unchanged.

"It was a really big number and a really bad number. From the political standpoint, it is clearly a number that will put pressure on the government to take quick measures," said Eric Chaney, an economist at Morgan Stanley.
The Socialist government came to power in a parliamentary election on June 1, ousting the centre-right, on a pledge to put fighting unemployment at the top of its political agenda.
Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has set a goal of creating 700,000 jobs over the next couple of years, half of them in the public sector.
